name: OPA1602 / OPA1604 (TI SoundPlus dual/quad bipolar-input, 2.5 nV/√Hz)
tagline: TI's 2011 SoundPlus bipolar dual/quad: 2.5 nV/√Hz and 0.00003% THD+N at 2.6 mA/ch. TI support steered LME49720 users to it, and OEMs use it for I/V and line stages.
technology: Bipolar-input, rail-to-rail-output, unity-gain-stable voltage-feedback op-amp (TI SoundPlus line; the datasheet carries the Burr-Brown Audio logo). Surface-mount only: SOIC-8/MSOP-8 (VSSOP, DGK) for the dual, SOIC-14/TSSOP-14 for the quad.

reputation.summary: An OEM and engineering favourite rather than an op-amp-rolling legend. It comes only in SMD packages, so enthusiasts rarely swap it. It pairs low noise and distortion with modest supply current (2.6 mA/ch). Per a TI E2E thread and Gearspace discussion (not re-checked this run), TI pointed LME49720 users to it after that part's EOL. Reported design wins come from mirrored reviews (Soomal, Frieve) and maker pages: the iBasso DX90 uses a pair of OPA1602 per channel as the DAC I/V stage (with OPA1611 and BUF634), and the Cayin RU3 dongle uses OPA1602 alongside SGM8262 in parallel drive. DIY projects use it as a transformerless balanced line driver, and the quad OPA1604 shows up in multichannel mixers. No op-amp-specific listening tests or ASR/Samuel Groner measurements were found.
sonic_descriptors: neutral, restrained, relaxed, slightly soft mids: Soomal's description of the whole iBasso DX90 player, not of the op-amp alone
typical_uses: DAC I/V conversion (iBasso DX90, per Soomal)
Portable DAC/headphone dongle output stage in parallel drive (Cayin RU3)
Replacement for the LME49720/LM4562 in new designs (TI support suggestion per E2E, unconfirmed this run)
Transformerless balanced line driver (DIY XPS project)
Multichannel line mixers and filter banks (OPA1604)
caveats: SMD only (SOIC/MSOP/TSSOP). A DIP-8 socket needs an adapter board.
About ±30 mA output drive suits line level, not low-impedance headphones on its own. The designs above add BUF634s or parallel sections.
Current noise of about 1.8 pA/√Hz (TI figure) makes noise rise with high source impedances, a general bipolar-input trade-off.
No op-amp-specific stability or oscillation reports were found.

revision_history.changes: Initial release, dated from the 'APRIL 2011' origin in the SBOS474B header. No copy was identified; radiolocman di=107868 is a candidate. Unconfirmed.
Existence inferred from TI's lettering sequence. A targeted search for 'SBOS474A' found no copy or change log. Unconfirmed.
Current revision as of Sept 2026 (ti.com symlink PDFs). Searches for C/D/E found nothing. The A→B change-log text was not seen. There is no sign of an electrical re-spec or new silicon.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remark reports specific to OPA1602/OPA1604 were found. As an SMD part it is often sold on marketplaces pre-mounted on DIP-8 adapter boards, where the chip's origin cannot be checked. Buy from authorized distributors (TI, DigiKey, Mouser) and check the top-side marking and lot trace code with TI's marking lookup.

open_questions: Contents of the SBOS474 initial (Apr 2011) and SBOS474A revisions, and the A→B change log, are still unseen. radiolocman di=107868 (OPA1602AID) and the alldatasheet 437564/437565 copies are candidates for older frozen revisions.

No OPA1602/OPA1604-specific PCN surfaced. TI's 150 mm-to-RFAB/FFAB/MIHO8 fab-migration PCNs (2024–2025, which include die revisions) did not list these parts in the search summaries. Check TI's PCN database for SBOS474 orderables. PCN20230613005 (TSSOP symbolization update) may or may not cover OPA1604AIPWR.

revision_chain_notes:
Texas Instruments SBOS474 (OPA1602/OPA1604, sole source, no second sources or acquirer re-issues known), oldest to newest:
(1) SBOS474, initial issue, April 2011. MISSING: no copy confirmed. Candidates are radiolocman di=107868 (already listed) and Wayback captures of the focus.ti.com / ti.com symlink or sbos474 URLs from April to November 2011.
(2) SBOS474A, between April and November 2011. MISSING: a targeted search for 'SBOS474A' OR 'SBOS474C' OR 'SBOS474D' found no copy, date or change log. Its existence is inferred only from TI's lettering.
(3) SBOS474B, 'APRIL 2011 – REVISED NOVEMBER 2011'. Present, confirmed again this run. It is still the live ti.com symlink or GPN document, and search summaries again identified it as SBOS474B.
No revision C, D or E turned up. The OPA1602/OPA1604 datasheet shows no sign of newer revisions or a silicon change.
New copies this run: ti.com/lit/gpn/opa1602, radiolocman di=305455 (OPA1604), the alldatasheet view page for 437564, datasheetspdf.com, GlobalSpec (OPA1604AID), and two more digchip URLs. None of their search summaries showed a revision letter, so all are marked low confidence (the GPN link is medium).
The archive seeds follow TI's standard legacy URL patterns (focus.ti.com symlink and per-revision /lit/ds/sbos474x/ paths). They are unverified candidates for Wayback lookup of the initial and A revisions, not confirmed live documents.
Budget: 3 WebSearch calls were issued. Two returned results; the third was refused because the session-wide search budget (200/200) was exhausted, so no distributor copies (Mouser, Digi-Key, Farnell, LCSC) were searched.
